subject.title: Gateway restart drops queued and in-flight inbound messages

question: Which restart-recovery architecture should own this issue: the SQLite followup-queue candidate, the SIGUSR1 drain mitigation, or a successor design that combines durable followups with channel-level replay?
rationale: The source issue is valid, but the requested behavior spans core gateway shutdown, process-local followup queues, durable state, and channel acknowledgment contracts; an automated fix would risk duplicating or conflicting with the existing open PRs.

options.title: Advance a SQLite-backed successor
options.body: Use the existing SQLite followup-queue PR as the base or replacement, require upgrade-safe storage and live channel proof, and fold in drain-window replay semantics before closing this issue.

options.title: Split the phases
options.body: Land a narrow followup persistence or SIGUSR1 drain fix first, then leave downtime catch-up and channel ACK deferral to the broader restart-recovery issues.

options.title: Pause the branch set
options.body: Close or pause the current broad PRs if maintainers want a redesigned core/plugin API before any durable replay work lands.

recommendation.title: Advance a SQLite-backed successor
recommendation.body: Use the existing SQLite followup-queue PR as the base or replacement, require upgrade-safe storage and live channel proof, and fold in drain-window replay semantics before closing this issue.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged work on gateway restart drain makes this the strongest routing signal for the architectural choice.
